title: Landing-page documentation and legal links resolve to the current page instead of real targets
reasoning: Several visible calls to action and footer resource/legal links use href="#". In a deployed landing page, clicking these links does not navigate to documentation, installation, changelog, license, or terms content; it either stays on the same page or jumps to the top depending on browser behavior. This is user-facing broken navigation, and it is especially misleading for documentation/install links that are presented as primary next steps.
reproduction: Open the landing page and click Read Documentation, Documentation, Installation, Changelog, License, or Terms. The URL target is just # rather than a real route or document.
recommendation: Replace placeholder href="#" values with real routes or external documentation URLs. If some pages do not exist yet, remove the links or label them as unavailable rather than shipping dead navigation.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the included package test command is generic; there is no evidence of a landing-page navigation/link integrity test.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a landing-page render test that collects visible anchors in CTAFooter and asserts resource/legal CTAs do not use '#' placeholders unless explicitly marked disabled.
minimumFixScope: Update CTAFooter link targets for documentation, installation, changelog, license, and terms, or remove unavailable links.
